prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, bringing optical frequency standards to the 1e-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep the optical lattice clock as my preferred configuration after the full first-round exchange and the chair's questions. The achievement is one invention with a precise physical content: Katori's magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift so that many atoms can be held without Doppler or recoil broadening and without perturbing the clock transition, and Ye's group showed how far that scheme can be pushed, to fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 with ultrastable lasers and clock-to-clock comparisons. The citation rests on a measured quantity that Tokyo, Boulder, Braunschweig, Paris and other laboratories have reproduced and compared, so it does not depend on an interpretation that could later be revised. All eight members proposed the same two names for it, which is unusual and leaves the attribution question about what lies outside the pair, not about the pair. As to the chair's criterion question, my own criterion is a discovery or invention that is sharply defined, independently confirmed and stable in its meaning; on that test B007 is stronger today than B001, even though I grant that B001 opened the broader field. I also hold that the lattice clock is not a refinement of the 2005 or 2012 prizes: the comb is a frequency-counting tool, ion control concerns single trapped quantum systems, and the lattice clock's gain comes from interrogating very many neutral atoms at once with the light shift engineered away, which is a different mechanism and a different error budget.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged: a committee could regard the lattice clock as precision engineering on pillars that are already honoured, the comb (2005) and ion control (2012), and the largest payoff, the redefinition of the second, has not yet been decided, so part of the impact is prospective. I would not make that redefinition a condition of maturity, since the physical achievement is complete without it, but it is a fair point against anyone who wants the payoff realised first. Credit also leaks: the ultrastable cavity lasers and the Sr and Yb lattice-clock work of other groups (for example Ludlow, Hinkley, Campbell, Takamoto) lie outside two names and the three-name limit cannot absorb them. The most serious argument against my position is the one the chair records, that B001 has six explicit supporters in round 1 against two for B007, and that it opened a larger area of physics. I do not treat the support count as a scientific argument either way, and I have not seen a round-1 argument that the lattice clock is scientifically weak, but I accept that a committee weighing field-opening breadth above sharpness of attribution could reasonably choose B001.

responses.point: Danielsson argues that the flat-band prediction followed by experiment is a falsifiable sequence in which nature supplied the clue, that the existence of flat-band correlated phases does not depend on the pairing mechanism, and that B001 opens a new class of matter while B007 refines an honoured field.
responses.response: I accept the first part completely: the 2011 continuum model followed by the 2018 observations is the cleanest prediction-then-experiment sequence on the list, and independent reproduction is real. Our difference is what the citation would claim. The phrase 'correlated-insulator and superconducting states' invites the reader to take the phases as the established content, while the nature of the superconductivity and of several correlated states is still contested, and the committee would have to word the citation very carefully to avoid implying an explanation. My second disagreement is with 'refines an honoured field'. The comb prize recognised a way to count optical frequencies, and the lattice clock is a separate trapping scheme with its own physics, in which the light-shift cancellation and the many-atom interrogation are the invention. That is not an improvement of the comb in the way a better comb would be. I have not moved, but your point that B001 opens more physics is the strongest argument for it, and I rate it as a question of criterion and not of correctness.

responses.point: Mehlig now names Bistritzer with MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero for B001, but acknowledges that the experimental credit is unresolved and that the clock has the cleaner attribution and mature, reproduced performance, so he lists B007 as a fallback.
responses.response: I agree that three names is the defensible set for B001 and that dropping Bistritzer would break the logic of crediting the prediction, so I withdraw any suggestion of a two-name B001 from my own thinking. Your own account of the asymmetry, though, is the reason I stay with B007: a clean pair for the clock against an experimental side of B001 that remains split among Jarillo-Herrero, Cao, Fatemi and others, and a prediction with precursors. I would add that your point about a theory-experiment sequence cuts both ways. The clock is also invention followed by demonstration, with Katori's concept and Ye's performance, and the demonstration is independently reproduced. The remaining difference between us is how much weight an unsettled mechanism deserves, and since you say the field could look early if the mechanism turns out otherwise, I think we are closer than our rankings suggest.

responses.point: Olsson moved to B001 from B030, argues that the Nobel-relevant discovery is the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated phases and not a settled mechanism, and says eight years of independent confirmation is mature enough.
responses.response: Your reframing helps: if the citation is confined to the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated phases at that angle, the unsettled-mechanism objection is much weaker, and I take that seriously as an answer to the chair's second question. What I still cannot resolve is the experimental credit. You list Cao, the Fatemi and Dean-type independent experiments and earlier twisted-graphene theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Suarez Morell) as unresolved, and I think those are not minor wording matters but part of who made the discovery. The clock has an equivalent leak in the other Sr and Yb groups, but those groups followed the Katori and Ye demonstrations and do not precede them. I also note that your point that a combination of B001 and B007 is impossible within three names removes the compromise, so the committee has to choose, and I choose the case where attribution is not in dispute.

responses.point: Kroll, who also prefers B007, discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory and a possible link to Jun Ye through JILA, and stresses that the capability to measure changed.
responses.response: On the chair's recusal question I would say disclosure, as Kroll has done, and recording of the Hall and JILA links in the minutes is sufficient, since Hall is not among the names and a laboratory stay is not a collaboration with Ye; if Kroll finds a closer personal tie to Ye he should decide for himself. That means a vote on B007 should be seen to be carried by more than the two members who prefer it, and I note that all six others list B007 as an alternative. I also keep my earlier qualification: Ye's contribution is the stability record and the many-body clock physics, not a continuation of the comb work, so I would not reduce his credit to that of an infrastructure provider. I am slightly less certain than Kroll that the capability argument should carry the case alone, because a committee that prizes field-opening discovery will not be moved by it, and I would rather say so than hide it.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, supports B001 but names B007 as the cleaner and more mature alternative if the committee judges the interpretation of B001 too unsettled, with a precise two-person attribution and measurable payoff.
responses.response: Your conditional is close to my own position. I agree that the flat-band phases do not depend on the pairing mechanism, in the way earlier prizes did not wait for a complete theory, and I do not claim that B001 is premature in the sense of unconfirmed. My concern is narrower: the credit problem you yourself name, that Cao, Fatemi and the confirming groups fall outside three names, and the sample-to-sample disorder you mention, leave more for a later commentator to dispute than anything on the B007 side. If the committee decides that the choice between the two is to be settled by cleanliness of attribution and stability of interpretation, B007 is ahead; if by field-opening breadth, B001 is ahead. I would be willing to defend B001 as a fallback, and that is why it is my first alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will weigh field-opening breadth above sharpness of attribution, in which case B001 would rightly come first.
Whether the not-yet-completed redefinition of the second should be treated as a maturity condition or an adjacent policy matter; I treat it as adjacent but accept the argument is open.
Whether other Sr and Yb lattice-clock groups and the ultrastable-laser developers have credit claims that two names cannot reflect.

Whether the interpretation of the correlated and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene will settle enough, and whether the experimental credit can be fixed within three names, to change my ranking of B001 against B007.
statement.conflict_note: For B007 (Katori, Ye) I find no specific conflict in my profile; my documented ties are to the Lund attosecond group, Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich, Anne L'Huillier and others, none of whom is among the names credited on B007 or B001. I support Kroll's disclosure of his Hall and JILA links being recorded and see no need for recusal on B007 for me. If B008 or B015 were taken up, my professional proximity to ETH Zurich (Esslinger) and to atomic theory around Zoller and Cirac should be noted and discussed. No recusal is needed on my part for the configuration I propose.
